# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 88 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Athous, Shepherd of Hermas 88 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_088_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 9 — The Great Allegory Explained

**1** The Shepherd came and asked the virgins, "Did you treat him well?" "Ask him yourself," they said. "Lord," I told him, "I was so glad to be with them." **2** "What did you eat?" he asked. "Lord," I said, "I feasted on the words of the Lord all night long." **3** "Did they take good care of you?" "Yes, Lord, they did." **4** The Shepherd smiled. "Do you know who the tall man is?" "No, Lord." "He is the Son of God," he said. **5** "Then why does he appear so tall?" I asked. "Because he is taller than the tower itself," he answered. **6** "And the gate, Lord — what does that mean?" "That gate is the Son of God," he said. "It is the only way in to the Lord. No one comes to him except through his Son. **7** Do you remember the six men you saw, with the great and glorious angel standing in the center? He is the Son of God, and the six are the magnificent angels who stand at his right and left. **8** Not one of those glorious angels enters the presence of God except through him. Anyone who refuses to take his name on themselves cannot enter the kingdom of God." **9** "And the tower?" I asked. "The tower is the Church," he said. **10** "And who are the virgins?" "They are holy spirits. No one can be found in God's kingdom unless these virgins have clothed them. If you claim the name but don't receive their clothing, it does you no good. **11** "And what are those white garments of the virgins?" "They are their names," he said. "If someone bears the name of the Son of God and also bears all these names — the names of the virtues — they will enter the kingdom of God."

---

*PNEUMA makes the christological key explicit: "No one comes to him except through his Son" echoes John 14:6. The dual requirement — name plus garment — is rendered clearly.*
